source_text: Interibit Manichaeorum memoria cum strepitu, quia Dominus in aeternum permanet, qui paravit in iudicio sedem suam et ipse iudicabit orbem terrarum in aequitate [n176] . Nullum est in Deo crimen. Non igitur creat malos, quoniam, si mali essent natura, Deus eos creare non posset; ac per hoc, ut catholicorum est confiteri Deum conditorem bonorum, ita Manichaeorum proprie Deum credere conditorem malorum.
pass_a_gloss: The memory of the Manichaeans will perish with a crash, because the Lord remains into eternity, who has prepared in judgment his seat and he himself will judge the orb of lands in fairness. There is no crime in God. He therefore does not create evils, since, if they were evils by nature, God could not create them; and through this, as it is of catholics to confess God the founder of goods, so it is properly of Manichaeans to believe God the founder of evils.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: The Manichaeans’ memory will perish with a crash, because ‘the Lord remains forever; he has prepared his throne for judgment, and he himself will judge the world with fairness’ (Psalm 9:6–8; LXX/Vulgate Psalm 9:7–9) (Psalm 9:6–8;). There is no crime in God. He therefore does not create evil people: if they were evil by nature, God could not create them. Consequently, just as confessing God as creator of good beings belongs to catholics, believing God the creator of evil beings belongs specifically to Manichaeans.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
